output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, the newest specifically identified case is Muller v. DoorDash, Inc., a putative TCPA class action filed in the Southern District of Florida on November 9, 2026; the docket shows the complaint was filed but no merits ruling. DoorDash is also defending Oller v. DoorDash, Inc. in Indiana, where the Court of Appeals on September 18, 2026 reversed dismissal of a negligence claim alleging that DoorDash’s business model and app encouraged unsafe driving; a separate Pennsylvania hit-and-run injury suit against DoorDash and Uber Eats ended in a confidential settlement on October 29, 2026. Other current or recently filed matters include proposed consumer class actions in British Columbia over mandatory added delivery fees and in California over DashPass “$0 delivery fee” advertising, plus the Browne v. DoorDash administrative discrimination proceeding. DoorDash’s latest 10-Q says its broader ongoing matters include Dasher-independent-contractor classification claims and arbitrations, consumer/competition/data-protection/civil-rights matters, intellectual-property claims, personal-injury cases, and a California EDD payroll-tax audit; it says no disclosed proceeding is expected to have a material effect individually, while warning outcomes are uncertain.
caveats: This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of every individual Dasher arbitration, personal-injury claim, or other ordinary-course matter; DoorDash’s latest filing describes categories rather than naming every case.

The Muller, British Columbia, California DashPass, and Browne matters had limited publicly available procedural information in the opened sources; allegations are not findings of liability. The Pennsylvania case is reported as settled confidentially, so its terms are unavailable.

DoorDash states in its latest 10-Q that litigation outcomes are inherently unpredictable and that no disclosed proceeding is expected to have a material effect on its financial position or profitability individually.

output.question: What lawsuits is DoorDash involved in?

key_facts.fact: Muller v. DoorDash, Inc. is a TCPA class action filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida on November 9, 2026; the docket records the complaint filing.
In Oller v. DoorDash, Inc., the Indiana Court of Appeals reversed the trial court’s dismissal of an independent-negligence claim and remanded the case.
A Pennsylvania civil suit alleging DoorDash and Uber Eats were liable for a delivery driver’s hit-and-run injury ended in a confidential settlement.

A proposed British Columbia consumer class action alleges DoorDash adds mandatory fees after advertising a lower delivery price; the case update says the parties attended a judicial management conference on September 16, 2026.

A California proposed class action filed April 15, 2026 alleges DoorDash charged mandatory service fees on DashPass orders advertised as having $0 delivery fees; the source says the case remained pending and no class had been certified or settlement reached.
Michael Browne v. DoorDash, Inc., OCAHO Case No. 2026B00020, remained an active administrative proceeding reflected in an October 22, 2026 order concerning substitution of complainant’s counsel.

DoorDash’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 identifies ongoing Dasher-classification claims, consumer/competition/data-protection/civil-rights matters, intellectual-property matters, personal-injury matters, and a California EDD payroll-tax audit.
